title: Relationships: Mindsets in Love (or Not)
coreMove: In love, friendship, and social life, growth means interpreting pain in ways that preserve repair, boundaries, accountability, and future learning.

exampleSpecs.stakes: pain could harden into shame or revenge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: anchor in breakup and rejection interviews to separate pain from permanent identity

exampleSpecs.stakes: ordinary imperfection may be mistaken for fatal mismatch
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Penelope to show small traits becoming total dismissal

exampleSpecs.stakes: one awkward exchange may stop future practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: anchor in Jennifer Beer shyness study to treat social skill as developable

exampleSpecs.stakes: ranking may turn insecurity into contempt
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use adolescent boys and gender stereotypes to show fixed ranking moving outward

exampleSpecs.stakes: hurt may turn into identity and retaliation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Columbine and Brooks Brown to separate hurt from revenge identity

exampleSpecs.audience: friends feeling diminished by another person’s success
exampleSpecs.stakes: envy could poison a valued friendship
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: connect friendship success envy to the relational mindset and fixed ranking
